title: Scale the registry_v2 loss-aware logit path beyond the 16/8 prompt slice
description: resattn-7mb doubled the oracle-alpha pilot split by introducing prompts/registry_v2.yaml with 16 pilot prompts and the same 8 confirm prompts. title: Scale compact-subword Figure 8 proxy beyond tokenizer-only regime

title: Decide whether to revisit Figure 8 via a more faithful proxy or freeze the strong-claim lane

Decide whether the strong Figure 8 / trained-routing lane should remain frozen at the current descriptive boundary or be revisited through a more faithful proxy path, such as a larger local reproduction or another open depth-mixing comparison with released weights.

title: Review held-out oracle-alpha predictiveness design after prompt and hybrid features fail
description: resattn-27f compared prompt-shape baselines, mean token-embedding baselines, and hybrids that appended those features to the best token-aware h_4[t] summary. None of them beat the existing position_thirds_mean_pooled_h_4[t]_resid_post_layer_3_concat baseline on pilot leave-one-out JS, so the confirm result stayed unchanged and still slightly below uniform on predicted routed loss. Next step is a bounded design review of the held-out predictiveness setup: whether the sequence-level alpha target is too coarse, whether the linear ridge model is the wrong predictor family, whether the prompt slice is too small for the current dimensionality, and whether JS tuning is misaligned with the routed-loss objective.
close_reason: Completed bounded predictiveness design-review alignment; logged follow-up resattn-qq2 for constrained or compressed targets.

title: Compare prompt-level and hybrid feature surfaces for oracle-alpha predictiveness
description: resattn-7ve showed that coarse token-aware h_4[t] summaries help held-out alpha similarity a bit: position_thirds_mean_pooled_h_4[t]_resid_post_layer_3_concat beat the pooled baselines on pilot leave-one-out JS and modestly improved confirm R^2 and mean JS. But predicted routed loss stayed effectively neutral to slightly below uniform on average, so the Phase 1 held-out predictiveness blocker remains open. Next compare small prompt-level baselines and hybrid prompt-shape plus internal-state summaries on the pilot split only, then rerun confirm without changing the saved prompt registry.
close_reason: Completed prompt-level and hybrid oracle-alpha feature comparison; logged follow-up resattn-23p for predictiveness design review.

title: Implement Gemma routed-vs-original factual-recall tool-breakage baseline
description: Build the first same-model Gemma-2 factual-recall tool-breakage runner using the custom tuned-lens baseline from resattn-5k9 and the metric hierarchy from resattn-ehz. Compare original-model versus routed-model traces under both raw logit lens and tuned lens, treat held-out KL as the primary tuned-lens baseline metric, report mean/final-position diagnostics, and preserve the requirement for a later controlled dynamic-routing counterfactual before any strong claim.
close_reason: Landed checkpointed Gemma routed-vs-original factual-recall baseline runner, pilot artifact, and control-doc updates; follow-up resattn-ypj tracks stronger relative success metrics before confirm.

description:

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Resolve held-out target tradeoff after compressed oracle-alpha comparison
description: resattn-3ns implemented a deterministic depth/type-band compressed target with train-derived lift-back templates and compared it against the existing full-source logit target on the saved pilot/confirm split. The compressed target improved confirm R^2 and mean JS relative to the full-source logit target and selected a tiny ridge penalty, but it lost the positive routed-loss gain that the full-source logit target had recovered. The next bounded step is to decide the confirm decision metric explicitly and compare the next minimal redesign, such as alternative lift-back schemes, hybrid targets, or another target family, against that criterion.
notes: Duplicate of resattn-xaa; keep resattn-xaa as the canonical oracle-alpha follow-up because CURRENT_STATE and the new artifact write-up already point to loss-aware selection as the next bounded redesign.

title: Optimize held-out predictiveness ridge solves for the n<<d regime
description:
## Why
`resattn-js8` completed successfully, but the current ridge helper solves the primal `(d + 1) x (d + 1)` system for each leave-one-out fold even when the prompt count is much smaller than the feature dimension. On the primary Gemma `96 / 128` run this turned a valid bounded check into a roughly hour-long numerical sweep with no progress visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The ridge helper uses an `n << d`-appropriate formulation or otherwise removes the current high-dimensional primal bottleneck.
- The predictiveness path preserves existing metrics and artifact semantics.
- A targeted timing or regression artifact shows the new path materially reduces wall-clock on the saved prompt surface.

description: The best-checkpoint widened compact-subword wikitext-103 artifact from resattn-fby shows the current local Block AttnRes proxy reaches a healthier early regime under the standard next-token objective, but does not sustain a routed win or the Figure 8 entropy ordering. Before any objective-level change, run a bounded matched regularization sweep on the same widened wikitext-103 setup with tokenization, corpus, width, sequence length, and objective fixed. Use the existing best-checkpoint-enabled runner and compare the current control (already saved at dropout=0.0, weight_decay=0.01) against three new settings: (1) dropout=0.1, weight_decay=0.01, (2) dropout=0.0, weight_decay=0.05, and (3) dropout=0.1, weight_decay=0.05. Judge each arm by best-checkpoint baseline-vs-AttnRes loss delta and the Figure 8 entropy gap. If no regularization arm restores a routed win or materially improves the entropy ordering beyond the current best-checkpoint artifact, objective-level redesign becomes the next live question.

title: Implement constrained or compressed oracle-alpha predictiveness target
description: resattn-23p aligned the runner with the saved predictiveness metrics and added prompt-matched per-sequence stability reporting, but it did not change the core blocker identified by external review: the current predictiveness path still learns raw oracle-alpha simplex targets in unconstrained Euclidean ridge coordinates, with an 8/8 prompt split that is tiny relative to target dimension. Add a v2 predictiveness formulation that either predicts constrained alpha logits / logistic-normal coordinates or a compressed target such as block mixtures or top-k support, and wire the control plan explicitly to that path before rerunning held-out experiments.
notes: Implemented the alpha-logit predictiveness target path, reran the held-out check on gpt2-xl, and opened resattn-3ns for compressed-target follow-up after the mixed result.

title: Freeze dependencies and start Phase 1 reconstruction checks
close_reason: Pinned the direct and transitive Phase 1 dependency set, installed the scientific stack into .venv with MPS available, and added the first reconstruction/cache-validity validation suite. Follow-up model-backed validation is tracked in resattn-ydp.

title: Analyze prereg-scale GPT-2 XL oracle routing patterns
description: The registry_v4 prereg-scale campaign on gpt2-xl completed on 96 pilot and 128 confirm prompts. The oracle stage clears the development-model Phase 1 oracle gate versus uniform and the preregistered nulls, while held-out predicted routed loss stays positive but alpha-shape metrics remain weak. Use the saved v4 artifact to start the next oracle lane: characterize routing-pattern structure at prereg scale, quantify descriptive summaries that are valid at the sequence level, and decide what can move into Phase 2 pattern analysis without overstating the current development-model result.
close_reason: Landed the first prereg-scale sequence-level pattern-analysis slice: reusable average-linkage JSD clustering helpers, runner script, and the GPT-2 XL registry_v4 artifact. The result shows weak above-random structure but stays below the prereg silhouette gate and is outlier-driven, so follow-up moved to resattn-ojq.

title: Make oracle-alpha predictiveness selection loss-aware after target tradeoff
description: resattn-3ns compared a compressed depth-type-band logit target against the current full-source logit target on the same feature surface. The compressed target improved confirm R^2/JS and eliminated ridge saturation, but lost the positive held-out routed-loss gain; the full-source logit target kept the only positive routed-loss result but had worse descriptive alpha metrics and still saturated at lambda=100. Add the next bounded redesign around selection or tuning that treats routed-loss recovery as the primary objective when comparing targets and regularization, while keeping descriptive alpha metrics as secondary diagnostics.
notes: Implemented loss-aware pilot tuning with multi-target comparison support, ran the bounded gpt2-xl comparison on the fixed token-aware feature surface, and recorded that the new selection rule still picked the raw-simplex target and stayed slightly negative on confirm. Open follow-up: resattn-7mb.

title: Add model-backed Phase 1 reconstruction and cache-validity checks
description: Extend the current validation module from toy linear-algebra checks to model-backed cache extraction and uniform-routing reconstruction on the development model. This should verify sublayer output accounting, final-normalization-aware reconstruction, and cache-validity identities on a real backend before broader oracle-alpha optimization.
close_reason: Added TransformerLens-backed model validation, including residual and logit reconstruction tests, a reusable smoke script, and a passing gpt2-xl MPS artifact for the configured development model.

title: Codify routed-vs-original Gemma tool-breakage success metrics before confirm run
description: Use the saved resattn-28b pilot artifact to harden the tool-breakage decision surface before any confirmatory Gemma factual-recall run. The current pilot baseline works and shows broad KL degradation under routing, but the prereg boolean non-monotonicity metric is saturated on the original-model baseline, so the next step must define explicit relative metrics such as routed-vs-original target-rank degradation or other trace-instability summaries and then reuse the cached pilot traces to validate them.
close_reason: Landed relative routed-vs-original Gemma tool-breakage metrics, regenerated the saved pilot summary from checkpoints, updated the pilot memo/control docs, and opened resattn-6te for the confirm run.
